title: Fine-Tuned Model Deployment
learning_outcomes: Explain model versioning and artifact storage and how it connects to fine-tuned model deployment.
Apply inference compatibility in the example and predict the output before running it.
Test one realistic edge case for fine-tuned model deployment and explain what the example does not prove.

content.intro: This lesson covers fine-tuned model deployment through 6 syllabus subtopics preserved from the supplied Generative AI curriculum. Customize an existing model only after establishing a baseline and deciding prompting or retrieval is insufficient. Dataset permissions, compute, evaluation, and versioned artifacts all matter.

Trace its inputs, the operation or decision it describes, the result a learner can observe, and the limitations that matter for the intended task. Confirm the idea with a small example and an explicit check rather than relying on fluent or plausible output.

items.text: Use inference compatibility to reason about behavior under real workloads, not just a successful local example. Measure latency and cost on representative requests, define operational limits and rollback options, and test what happens when dependencies slow down or fail.

items.title: Access controls and license compliance
items.text: Access controls and license compliance requires a documented decision that fits the use case and jurisdiction. Identify affected stakeholders, distinguish binding obligations from voluntary guidance, retain evidence for the decision, and revisit the conclusion when the model, data, product, or applicable rules change.

items.title: Continuous evaluation after deployment
items.text: Use continuous evaluation after deployment to turn a vague quality claim into an observable criterion. Define a representative dataset, an expected outcome or rubric, a baseline, and the failure categories you will record; interpret aggregate scores alongside examples and affected groups.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Save the snippet to a local file such as lesson_example.py and run it with Python 3.11+ using `python lesson_example.py`. This is a local/static teaching example; CodeLeaf's current browser iframe previews HTML/CSS/JavaScript and is not a secure Python runner. Do not paste API credentials into the example or public source files.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original snippet and fixed sample inputs, rerun it, then change one input at a time and compare the new output with the stated contract.

content_blocks.title: Provider and version note
content_blocks.text: Model names, API payloads, supported modalities, quotas, pricing, and SDK behavior vary by provider and change over time. Treat linked official documentation as the authority for a live integration; examples here avoid hard-coded production model IDs and secrets.

content.task: Practice model versioning and artifact storage within fine-tuned model deployment: use a small synthetic input, predict the result, run the example, then change one input to test an edge case. Record the expected result and one limitation.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example uses a clearly described, non-sensitive input.
Expected behavior and at least one edge/failure case are written down.
The learner checks the result against an explicit criterion and records limitations.
hints: Begin with a tiny input whose expected behavior you can explain before running it.
Change one variable at a time and retain a fixed baseline for comparison.
When a model or external service is involved, inspect evidence and errors; do not treat the model response as a trusted instruction.

common_mistakes.mistake: Assuming fluent or plausible output is necessarily correct.
common_mistakes.fix: Use evidence, schema checks, representative test cases, and human review for consequential results.

common_mistakes.mistake: Changing several inputs or parameters at once.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep a baseline and vary one factor at a time so the effect can be interpreted.

common_mistakes.mistake: Putting secrets or private source material in prompts, logs, or a public example.
common_mistakes.fix: Use synthetic data, server-side secret storage, data minimization, and reviewed retention rules.

summary: Fine-Tuned Model Deployment is one part of a larger generative AI application lifecycle.
Use explicit inputs, criteria, and reproducible examples to test the concept.
Document uncertainty, failure modes, security considerations, and version assumptions.
